def load() -> pd.DataFrame:
    import pandas as pd

    path = "data/legal/input/csn-data-book-2024-csv/CSVs/2024_CSN_State_Top_Ten_Report_Categories.csv"
    # File has a title row, then a proper header row.
    df = pd.read_csv(path, skiprows=1, dtype=str)

    # If the header was not parsed (shows up as Unnamed columns with first row = header labels), fix it.
    if all(c.startswith("Unnamed") for c in df.columns) and len(df) > 0 and str(df.iloc[0, 0]).strip().lower() == "state":
        df.columns = df.iloc[0].tolist()
        df = df.iloc[1:].copy()

    # Drop trailing source/blank rows
    df = df.dropna(how="all")
    df["State"] = df["State"].astype(str).str.strip()
    df["Category"] = df["Category"].astype(str).str.strip()
    return df[["State", "Category", "# of Reports", "Percentage"]]

def process(topTenCategories):
    import pandas as pd

    df = topTenCategories.copy()

    # Remove footer / note rows (they have NaN for numeric-ish columns after standardization)
    df = df[df['# of Reports'].notna() & df['Percentage'].notna()]

    # Ensure report counts are usable for ordering
    df['reports'] = (
        df['# of Reports']
        .astype(str)
        .str.replace(',', '', regex=False)
        .str.strip()
    )
    df = df[df['reports'].str.fullmatch(r'\d+')]
    df['reports'] = df['reports'].astype(int)

    # For each state, find the top category by report count (tie-breaker: keep all tied max)
    max_per_state = df.groupby('State', as_index=False)['reports'].max().rename(columns={'reports': 'max_reports'})
    df2 = df.merge(max_per_state, on='State', how='inner')
    top_rows = df2[df2['reports'] == df2['max_reports']]

    # Keep states where Identity Theft is (one of) the top category/categories
    out = (
        top_rows[top_rows['Category'].str.strip().eq('Identity Theft')]
        [['State']]
        .drop_duplicates()
        .sort_values('State')
        .reset_index(drop=True)
    )

    return out
